$comment: PROPOSED manifest for the Yesan full-scale test site (Zenodo 21441974). NOT SCORING READY.
It holds NO targets: the record describes 'documented buried targets' and 'supporting ground-truth
information used in the accompanying MDPI Sensors publication', but no target list is in the held
files and the paper has not been found. The frames and open questions below record what the held
files DO establish, so that a target list, when obtained, lands in a structure that already says
why exact scoring would be unsafe until the line registration is resolved. No offset is guessed.
Investigated 2026-09-29: see docs/yesan-registration-investigation.md. Still no target list; registration unresolved.
title: Yesan full-scale bridge-transition test site (Korea Expressway Corporation Research Institute)

truth_source.record: Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.21441974 (CC-BY-4.0), 'Field Dataset for Complementary Subsurface Sensing Using a Quantum Diamond Magnetometer and Multi-Frequency Ground-Penetrating Radar at a Full-Scale Test Site', Oh, Chang-Geun (project leader)
held_files: Yesan test site GPR Raw data_0629.zip (MD5 6e40b0ea650b86d5802c5d393cc34c46, matches the record)
truth_source.missing: the target list (class, material, dimensions, burial depth, chainage, reference surface) from the MDPI Sensors paper or the authors
truth_source.gpr_acquisition_date: 2021-04-06 (zip member timestamps 14:42-15:23; inferred, not a header field)
truth_source.author_contact: Chang-Geun Oh, Hanseo University, coh@hanseo.ac.kr (verified: HUCAS faculty page and ORCID 0000-0002-9464-4397)

exhaustive.statement: No target list is held, so nothing can be attested exhaustive.

frames.origin: the authors' '0 m reference position', given per file as a trace number in 'summary of GPR data and formula.xlsx' (file 66: trace 65; 72: 96; 69: 107). What physical marker it is, is not documented in the held files.
frames.registration_note: Two distance scales disagree: the .rad wheel calibration gives 0.008429 m/trace (line A stops at 90.70-91.05 m) while the authors' sheet uses dx = 0.0086649550706 m/trace (93.23-93.59 m), about 2.8% longer and roughly 2.5 m over the line. Which one the target chainages use is unknown. The per-file 0 m trace (65/96/107) is where the authors put 0 m; its relation to the targets' chainage origin is unproven.

frames.origin: the authors' '0 m reference position', given per file as a trace number (file 68: trace 80; 74: 60; 71: 60). Physical marker undocumented.
frames.registration_note: Same two-scale disagreement as line A: .rad 0.008429 m/trace (89.17-89.97 m) vs sheet dx 0.0086649550706 m/trace (91.66-92.49 m).

open_questions.statement: The documented buried targets are not in any held file.
open_questions.resolution_route: the MDPI Sensors paper for this dataset, or the authors (project leader Oh, Chang-Geun)

open_questions.statement: The physical meaning of each file's '0 m reference position' trace, and whether target chainages are measured from it, is not established.
open_questions.resolution_route: authors, or a site drawing tying the 0 m marker to the target positions

open_questions.statement: The .rad interval 0.008429 m is 3 pulses / 355.9 pulses per metre; the authors' 0.0086649550706 m is 3 / 346.22, an unexplained re-calibration 2.8% longer. The published images use the authors' scale.
open_questions.resolution_route: authors: which distance calibration the published target chainages use

open_questions.statement: QDM file names put the approach slab at 30-60 m (line A, 2026), but the strongest GPR near-surface change is at 44.0-45.0 m (2021). A shared chainage (with the 44.5 m change inside the approach slab) and a ~14.5 m offset both fit the held evidence. Neither is adopted.

Every .rad header reads 'ANTENNAS:500 MHz shielded'. The folders say 250/500/800 MHz, and the evidence supports the folders: SIGNAL POSITION falls into three groups that coincide with the folder labels, and the recorded spectra have centroids of ~270, ~450 and ~715 MHz in the 250/500/800 folders. Inferred, not confirmed.
open_questions.resolution_route: authors; until then a frequency breakdown must cite the folder label, not the header

open_questions.statement: QDM repetition files name the same sections at other distances (approach slab_A_11-15 m, reinforced concrete_A_26-30 m, ascon_B_0-5 m), so at least two unstated distance conventions are in use.
Both lines probably run the same way (B repeats A's ~74 m change rather than mirroring it), but the physical start and end are not documented.

notes: Do not assign Grade A labels from this dataset until yesan-line-registration and yesan-distance-scale are resolved.
